card.headline: …my mind goes blank.
card.sub: “I can understand 100% of the video, but when I try to speak…”

beats.speech: I can understand 100% of the video, but when I try to speak, my mind goes blank.
Sound familiar? Well, don't worry, because your memory absolutely isn't broken.
First, in that blank moment, your brain is struggling to do exactly three jobs at once. Find the word, check if it fits, and build the grammar. It's total mental overload.
It's exactly why halfway through a job interview answer, you freeze.

quiz.q: A pub quiz. Your answer sheet is empty.
quiz.a_sub: You can't think of the answer.

beats.speech: Telling a story at dinner, you lose your train of thought.
And during a wedding speech, you stumble over your words.

Second, learning words inside full sentences does two of those jobs in advance. You already know the word's setting, so you know it fits. And you've already practised saying it, so the grammar is ready.

card.headline: One job left: find the word

beats.speech: Finally, this leaves only one job left. Finding the word. It arrives with its sentence already attached.

card.headline: “I was swamped at work this week.”

beats.speech: I was swamped at work this week.

card.headline: You don't need a better memory.
card.sub: You need words that come with their sentences.

beats.speech: You don't need a better memory. You just need to learn words that come with their sentences.
